source.description: Covariate models for mechanical parts: each part's failure rate is a base rate scaled by factors for the conditions it works in (load, speed, temperature, pressure, contamination, material and more), with the handbook's limits on every input. Seals, springs, solenoids, valves, bearings, gears, actuators, pumps, filters, brakes and clutches, compressors, electric motors, accumulators, fasteners, couplings, slider cranks, sensors, shafts, belt and chain drives, fluid conductors and miscellaneous parts.
caveats: CDNSWC (the Naval Surface Warfare Center, Carderock Division) and the U.S. Navy did not take part in making Reliafy and do not approve it. The handbook is the result of a research programme, not an official DoD document.
A handbook prediction model, not failures counted in service: never mix it with field data.
Each model is only as good as the conditions you give it. Outside the handbook's limits Reliafy refuses or warns, and says which limit and on which page.
The handbook says its equations were validated only in part, with limited funding: use it to compare designs and find the weak parts, not as a measure of how your equipment will fail.
Some rates are per million cycles or operations, not hours: a prediction needs how many there are an hour.

records.name: Bearing, rolling element (from its load rating)
records.label: Bearing, rolling element (from its load rating) (NSWC-11 Eq. 7-4)

failure_mode.name: Any failure
failure_mode.meaning: Its failure rate as the handbook models it: a base rate scaled by its conditions.

failure_modes: Fatigue damage: spalling, brinelling, smearing (heavy or prolonged load, excessive speed, shock, vibration)
Noisy bearing: surface fatigue, glazing, microspalling (loss of lubricant, housing out of round, corrosion)
Seizure: cracked rings or rolling elements, skidding (poor heat removal, loss of lubricant, high temperature)
Vibration: scuffing, fretting, pitting (misalignment, unbalanced or excessive load, poor housing support)
Electric currents: pits on raceways and balls

covariate_model.formula: λ_BE = λ_BE,B · C_R · C_ν · C_CW · C_t · C_SF · C_C, with λ_BE,B = 10⁶ / L10h and L10h = (10⁶ / 60n) · (L_S / L_A)^y
covariate_model.words: A rolling bearing's failure rate starts at one over its L10 life, the hours 90 % of bearings last at the load and speed it runs at (from its catalogue load rating). That is scaled by the reliability its life is quoted at, its lubricant's viscosity, water in the lubricant, its temperature, shock in service and dirt in its lubricant.

limits.why: a load rating is more than zero
the bearing needs a radial load

inputs.name: F_A
inputs.label: Axial (thrust) load
inputs.help: 0 for a pure radial load: L_A is then the radial load.

limits.why: the radial factor is more than zero
the thrust factor can't be negative

inputs.name: R
inputs.label: Reliability the life is quoted at
inputs.help: The handbook: use 50 % (the L50 life) to combine with other parts' MTBF-based rates.

inputs.name: nu_ratio
inputs.label: Viscosity of the specified lubricant ÷ viscosity of the one used

limits.why: a ratio of viscosities is more than zero

inputs.help: 1 when the bearing runs on the lubricant it was specified for (factor 1).

inputs.name: CW
inputs.label: Water in the lubricant

limits.why: a percentage of water is 0 to 100

inputs.help: 0 for a bearing designed for a water-based lubricant (the handbook: then C_CW = 1).

inputs.name: bearing_type
inputs.label: Bearing type
inputs.help: Sets the load-life exponent y: 3.0 for ball, 3.3 for roller.

choices.label: Uniform and steady load, free from shock
Extreme cleanliness: particles about the oil film thickness (laboratory)
High cleanliness: oil through a fine filter (10 micron or finer)
Normal cleanliness: slight contamination in the lubricant
Slight contamination: hard particles over 10 micron
Severe contamination: coarse filtering, no integral seals

checks.why: The axial load F_A should not exceed 30 % of the radial load F_R
